ruling: DERAILMENT, not de-rate. Management cut the FY26 revenue guide from $835-850M to $760-790M (-8.1% midpoint) on 2026-05-07, ninety days after setting it, converting FY26 from +6/+8% growth to -3.5%/+0.3%. Q2-26 is guided to -2.5% y/y. Estimates fell and the multiple followed. The queue's 'quality at own-history discount' frame is REFUTED: the 8.4% trailing-3y revenue CAGR that scored the name is dead (current +1.4%, forward -1.6%). Trap in growth costume.
cause: Two company-generated guidance events. (1) 2026-02-09 AMC Q4-25 print -> -19.1% on 02-10 (19.3M sh): FY26 guided +6/+8% revenue but Q1-26 adj EBITDA reset to $45-47M vs $52.9M just delivered. (2) 2026-05-07 AMC Q1-26 print -> -16.9% on 05-08 (26.6M sh, 52w low $7.44 set that day): FY26 revenue guide CUT 8.1%, 24% workforce reduction announced, $150M revolver commitment. No macro component.
honesty_note: The 2026-05-07 release is headlined 'GSV per Active Client Increased 5% Year-over-Year' and 'Company Raises Full Year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA Guidance'. Underneath: GSV -0.1%, active clients -3.4%, gross profit flat, gross margin -114bps, FCF -58%, and an 8.1% CUT to revenue guidance in the same release. The headline metric is an arithmetic consequence of a flat numerator over a shrinking denominator, and the EBITDA 'raise' is funded by firing 24% of the workforce. Every datum is disclosed; the marketed takeaway diverges from them by construction. Graded on divergence, not datum-disclosure, per doctrine.

A 37pp gap on a thesis resting on an undisclosed parameter is a disagreement we cannot adjudicate, not an edge. +14.7% E[edge] against 88.6% annualised IV and a +/-15-17% binary in seven days sits inside the noise. NO EDGE CLAIM.
plan: NO ENTRY. No band, no tranche, no starter. Score 3/10 is below the 4/10 band threshold. Re-court on any trigger in kill_triggers/re_court below.

mode_b_findings: Revenue growth is 100% take-rate and 0% marketplace volume. Take rate 19.51% (Q1-25) -> 19.80% (Q1-26): the +29bps contributed +$2.9M against an actual +$2.8M y/y revenue change, while GSV contributed -$0.1M. Verified from the company's own GSV and revenue figures.

The take-rate lever that masks GSV decline is the same lever that accelerates it - on a marketplace where buyer and seller know each other's identity, every basis point of take rate increases the payoff to transacting off-platform. A self-terminating masking channel whose terminal state is a revenue break, not a GSV break.

Non-AI GSV is shrinking ~2.5%/yr, derived and never printed. AI-related GSV ~$59M (Q1-25) -> ~$82M (Q1-26) at +40%, against total GSV flat, implies the other ~92% of the marketplace went ~$929M -> ~$905M. The entire equity value sits on the decay rate of that residual: at -2.5% total GSV inflects positive in 2027; at -6% it compounds down. Upwork does not disclose the parameter and structures disclosure so the subtraction is not done for you.
Take-rate expansion is not reaching gross profit - gross profit flat in dollars at $150.8M, gross margin -114bps. The price increase is consumed by cost of revenue.

Balance-sheet quality downgrade hidden by the 'net cash' framing: a previously unsecured net-cash company pledged substantially all assets to a secured revolver with maintenance covenants twelve days before a $361.0M maturity, while spending remaining liquidity on buybacks.

Governance thinness converging on the print: CFO on medical leave 2026-07-14 (CEO as interim PFO, return expected Q4-26) - removing the officer who set then cut the FY26 guide, 27 days before the print that tests it; GM Marketplace resigned 2026-03-12; two directors off at the June annual meeting.

AI-complex flag in the queue is wrong in the direction that matters: UPWK is not AI-capex-levered, it is an AI-WINS casualty. Entry does NOT require the AI cycle holding - it requires the cycle BREAKING. UPWK is a natural hedge to the household's ~$5.2M/26% AI-complex long book. That is the strongest honest argument for owning it, and it is insufficient at 3/10: buy AI-BREAK convexity directly, not through a derailed marketplace.

AMENDMENT - the direct estimate-revision test (per the parallel lane's _GATE_TEST_GUIDE_DECEL.md proposal) does NOT fire on UPWK: consensus FY26 EPS is UP 7.3% over 90 days. That does not reverse the ruling, it explains it - the de-rate-vs-derailment test splits by line, DERAILMENT on revenue and DE-RATE on earnings, because a 24% RIF raised EPS while revenue guidance was cut 8%. A stock whose EPS estimates rise while its revenue estimates fall, on cost cuts, with a forward year modelled to re-accelerate without any disclosed driver, is the classic setup for a step-down when the cost lever is exhausted. GENERALISABLE: always run the de-rate-vs-derailment test on BOTH the revenue and the earnings line - a single-line test would have graded this name backwards.

edge_explainer: Not an alpha claim - a documented exclusion plus a mechanism worth banking. The mechanism: on a two-sided marketplace where the parties know each other's identity, take-rate expansion is simultaneously the instrument that masks volume decline in the reported revenue line AND the strongest accelerant of off-platform leakage. Masking channel = take-rate expansion + a per-client ratio headline. Signal channel = active-client count and non-AI GSV, both disclosed and neither headlined. Signal-to-price latency ~1 quarter (the market repriced on the print both times, not before) - low latency means thin residual alpha, which is why this is DILIGENCE and not EDGE. Second banked observation: a company can be simultaneously an honestly-cheap 3.8x EV/EBITDA asset and an ELEVATE on disclosure architecture; those are independent axes and the court must score both.
unverifiable: TOP GAP: AI-related GSV is a management-defined, unaudited, unreconciled metric. The '>$300M annualized' and '+40%' figures anchor the entire non-AI decomposition. If the definition widened between Q4-25 and Q1-26, the -2.5% non-AI decay estimate is wrong in an unknown direction.

estimate_revision_test.note: THE SPLIT IS THE NAME. The de-rate-vs-derailment test returns OPPOSITE answers by line. ON REVENUE: DERAILMENT (company guide cut 8%, FY26 consensus -1.5%). ON EARNINGS: DE-RATE (consensus EPS rising, multiple compressed anyway). The Street's FY26 EPS is UP 7.3% since the May guidance cut because the 24% workforce reduction raised the EBITDA/EPS lines even as revenue was cut - the earnings are manufactured out of the cost base while the revenue base erodes, and the sell side has taken the bait, modelling FY27 revenue re-accelerating to +6.0% off a FY26 of -1.5% on the basis of nothing management has published. Hardens the DECLINE, and means the Aug-10 asymmetry is WORSE not better: the bar was raised (+2.4% on the quarter) while the business was not.
